rationale: I read the complete held working text of the order, both history observations (a 2026-10-15 Federal Register API disposition note and a 1989 printed codification row), and the acting text. The two observations are editorial leads and are not the basis; the basis is the acting instrument's own held text. EO 9866 (signed 1947-06-14, 12 FR 3909) designates the Under Secretary, ranking Assistant Secretary and Solicitor of the Interior to act as Secretary of the Interior in a stated order of succession (paragraph 1(a)-(c)), defines the ranking Assistant Secretary (paragraph 2), and in paragraph 3 supersedes Executive Order No. 9432. Executive Order 10156 (signed 1950-08-26, held text) re-issues the same three-step succession and ranking rule and states in its paragraph 3 that it supersedes Executive Order No. 9866 of June 14, 1947, entitled Designation of Officers To Act as Secretary of the Interior. The held text has no delayed effective date or savings clause, so every clause of 9866 was replaced on 1950-08-26. Paragraph 3 of 9866 (superseding 9432) is a spent supersession and not an independent continuing command. The supersession is express and names 9866, so it is not a recital. Earlier endings: none located in the held texts.
